name: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'
description: A semi-automatic shotgun chambered for Carrion's proprietary entropic munitions — shells containing a reactive chemical compound that destabilizes molecular bonds in the target material upon impact. The effect is visually dramatic: struck surfaces appear to age centuries in seconds, metal corroding, polymer crumbling, biological tissue necrotizing in a rapidly expanding circle around the wound channel. The compound has a limited active window of approximately four seconds before it becomes inert, preventing uncontrolled propagation, but within that window the damage is catastrophic and irreversible.
specifications:
gauge: Proprietary Carrion 14-gauge entropic shell
magazine: 6 rounds semi-automatic
effective range: 5-20 meters
compound active window: 4 seconds post-impact
necrotization radius: 8-12 cm from wound center
weight: 4.6 kg loaded
shelf life: Entropic shells degrade after 18 months
story_hooks: Expired entropic shells have been turning up in street markets — the degraded compound is unpredictable, sometimes activating on contact with skin rather than requiring ballistic impact.
A forensic chemist has reverse-engineered the entropic compound and published the formula on an open network — Carrion is scrambling to suppress it while simultaneously denying the weapon exists.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist semi-automatic shotgun with an aggressive, purposeful stance. The ES-4 'Ragnarok' reads as deliberately menacing — angular receiver, flared muzzle brake, and a prominent top-mounted rail system give it a predatory silhouette. The overall impression is industrial violence: compact, efficient, unapologetically lethal.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 98 cm | Barrel length: 51 cm | Receiver width: 8.5 cm | Stock depth: 32 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy when loaded (4.6 kg), with noticeable mass concentrated in the receiver and barrel assembly. Unloaded it sits at roughly 3.1 kg — substantial enough to command respect, balanced enough for practiced two-handed control despite the brutal recoil profile.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite receiver with steel internal components; barrel is hardened surgical steel with proprietary corrosion-resistant treatment (withstands the entropic compound's residual effects)
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with deliberate weathering patterns — scuffed edges, worn corners, surface micro-scratches suggesting field use. The barrel shows darker bluing in patches. Not pristine, but deliberately maintained.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charcoal polymer accents; heat-resistant black grip sections; dull steel hardware. Accent: deep crimson warning stripe along the magazine well and around the muzzle break — industrial hazard marking.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressive rubberized polymer grip with vertical grooves — designed for bare hand or light glove contact. Aggressive palm swell. The foregrip is wrapped in textured synthetic cord for secondary control.
distinctive_features: Proprietary Carrion 14-gauge shell magazine with visible ammunition count window (shells visible through smoked acrylic)
Vented muzzle brake with asymmetrical slots — aesthetically menacing, functionally manages the violent recoil from entropic detonation
Top-mounted Picatinny rail with factory iron sights (co-witness configuration)
Crimson warning stripe and biohazard-adjacent Carrion Defense Works triple-chevron logo laser-etched on receiver
Heat-dissipation vents along the barrel shroud (compound generates thermal bloom on activation)
Manual safety lever with tactile detent — positioned for thumb manipulation
Serial plate flush-mounted on receiver left side with micro-etched date code and batch number
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS triple-chevron logo embossed on left receiver above trigger guard. 'ES-4 RAGNAROK' stamped below the charging handle. Proprietary 'ENTROPIC CONTAINMENT SYSTEM' micro-etched on barrel shroud. Serial number and manufacture date on right receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The ES-4 is a precision tool for serious work — users keep it clean to maintain reliability, but the finish shows honest wear. Micro-scratches, minor scuffing on the stock, slight salt-corrosion patina on exposed steel components typical of Great Lakes climate exposure.
